speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the history of repetitive pivoting and twisting during volleyball, did you experience a specific "pop" sound or feeling of instability when the pain started? Also, can you point to the exact location of the pain on your knee and let me know if you have noticed any swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like pain on the inner part of your knee, near the tibial tubercle. Did you feel or hear a "pop" when the pain started, and does it hurt more when you bend your knee against resistance? Also, have you noticed any swelling or difficulty straightening your leg?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter Disease. The clinical presentation of tibial tubercle pain in a young female with recent increased physical activity and PCOS is highly specific to this overuse injury, ruling out meniscal tears or acute ligament injuries.
